faculty_junction_id.title: Deputy Director of Democracy and Good Governance Unit
faculty_junction_id.bio: Muhammad is a human rights activist and an expert in political technology. His work focuses on investigating, analyzing and advocating against human rights abuse linked to governments and international organizations. His goal is to end human rights abuses, especially in the Middle East, and to develop online rights mediating the relationship between humans and technology.
faculty_junction_id.short_bio: Muhammad Mokhtar is the Deputy Director of the Democracy and Good Governance Unit at Maat for Peace, Development and Human Rights.

faculty_id.title: Artificial Intelligence, Inequality and Inclusion in the Middle East and North Africa
faculty_id.description: In this lecture, Rizk unpacks the data ecosystem in the Middle East and North Africa, highlighting the unique demographic context of the region and its role in shaping the adoption and implementation of data and AI-based technologies. She begins by providing an important background around employment, poverty and inequality in the region before highlighting challenges around data infrastructure and technologies. Rizk later outlines rays of hope for data and AI use in the region. She concludes her lecture with a call for stakeholders to leverage AI and data to promote equality and inclusion.
faculty_id.short_description: In this lecture, Rizk unpacks the data ecosystem in the Middle East and North Africa, highlighting the unique demographic context of the region and its role in shaping the adoption and implementation of data and AI-based technologies.

faculty_junction_id.name: Nagla Rizk
faculty_junction_id.title: Professor of Economics
faculty_junction_id.bio:
Nagla’s area of research, teaching and advocacy is the economics of knowledge, technology and development, with focus on governance of data, responsible Artificial Intelligence, fair work in the platform economy, innovation, gender and inclusion in Egypt, the Middle East and North Africa (MENA). In her work as founding director of the Access to Knowledge for Development Center (A2K4D), Nagla is engaged with regional and international partners working on policy-oriented research that focuses on the developmental perspective of knowledge in general and knowledge governance in particular. 

Nagla also founded the Open Data for Development Node for the Middle East and North Africa. She leads the Feminist AI Research (f<a+i>r) network’s MENA hub, Open African Innovation Research Partnership (Open AIR)’s North Africa hub, and the Fairwork Egypt team, in partnership with Oxford Internet Institute. She is a Faculty Associate at Harvard’s Berkman Klein Center for Internet and Society, Affiliate Faculty at Harvard Law School’s CopyrightX course and an Affiliated Fellow of Yale Law School’s Information Society Project. She is an Associate Member at the University of Ottawa’s Centre for Law, Technology and Society.
faculty_junction_id.short_bio: Nagla Rizk is a Professor of Economics at The American University in Cairo, as well as the Founding Director of the Access to Knowledge for Development Center (A2K4D).

faculty_id.title: Understanding AI Governance through Games
faculty_id.description: In this module, Sundar introduces a unique approach to creating awareness of AI Governance and Ethics by incorporating games into the learning process. The use of games aims to provide a nuanced understanding of key concepts such as diversity, fairness, human agency, rights and freedom, accountability, causality, reliability, construct validity, data quality, and ethics. The advantage of using games is that they allow for experiential learning, the exploration of dynamic environments, and alignment with diverse cultural perspectives and lived experiences. The module will introduce 8 games, as well as constructs and tools to execute the games.
faculty_id.short_description: In this module, Sundar introduces a unique approach to creating awareness of AI Governance and Ethics by incorporating games into the learning process.

faculty_junction_id.name: Sundar Narayanan
faculty_junction_id.title: Consultant and Advisor - Ethics and Compliance, Fellow
faculty_junction_id.bio:
His primary experiences include advising companies on Ethics, Risk and Compliance frameworks, implementing monitoring mechanisms for risk and compliance, and formulating communication and training approaches to create awareness around organizational ethics and compliance standards. 

Sundar is also a researcher working on technology and data ethics. His research objective is focused on ”Tech Ethics: Culture, Controls and Compliance”. This includes the organizational behavior and cultural influence driving ethics and responsibility in AI development and deployment. He has spoken at forums on topics relating to data monetisation, data ethics and sustainability amongst others. In his spare time, Sundar hosts a successful podcast where he exchanges perspectives with professionals and experts from around the world.
faculty_junction_id.short_bio: Sundar Narayanan is an Ethics and Compliance professional with over 15 years of experience in providing advisory services to companies in India, the UAE, Japan, Kenya, Tanzania and Zambia.

faculty_id.title: AI and Ethics: Agriculture
faculty_id.description: Did you know that agribusinesses who sell farmers seeds and chemicals increasingly trade in big data and AI? Not unlike Facebook, Google and Amazon, companies such as Bayer/Monsanto use data collected via smart tractors with machine learning to derive insights on farming that they sell back to farmers. In this talk, Bronson will use empirical examples to develop a closely observed account of farm data collection and use with AI in the agri-food sector. Bronson will draw attention to agriculture as a high impact use case by walking through some of the potential ethical and social justice implications of AI in this sector. Ultimately, the talk will explore what could happen to food sovereignty and environmental justice if we do not anticipate the ethics of agricultural AI.
faculty_id.short_description: In this talk, Bronson will use empirical examples to develop a closely observed account of farm data collection and use with AI in the agri-food sector.

faculty_junction_id.name: Kelly Bronson
faculty_junction_id.title: Canada Research Chair in Science & Society
faculty_junction_id.bio: Kelly has published her work in national (Canadian Journal of Communication) and international journals (Science as Culture, Journal of Responsible Innovation, Big Data and Society). She has recently published a book on big data and AI in agriculture with McGill-Queen’s University Press titled, Immaculate Conception of Data: Agribusiness, activists and their shared politics of the future.
faculty_junction_id.short_bio: Kelly Bronson is a Canada Research Chair in Science & Society at University of Ottawa in Canada. She is a social scientist studying the societal and ethical dimensions of controversial technologies and their governance—from GMOs to big data and AI

faculty_id.title: AI, Art, and Ethics
faculty_id.description: With the rapid expansion of the use of generative AI, it is important to understand the implications of this emerging technology in different domains and sectors. In this module, Srinivasan explores the ethical challenges that emerge from the use of generative AI in the field of visual art, often referred to as generative art. Through a series of case studies, Srinivasan highlights existing biases in the field and shares specific tools that can drive the responsible development of art datasets and the use of ethical frameworks to assess the impact of AI systems.
faculty_id.short_description: In this module, Srinivasan explores the ethical challenges that emerge from the use of generative AI in the field of visual art, often referred to as generative art.

faculty_junction_id.name: Ramya Malur Srinivasan
faculty_junction_id.title: Senior Research Manager
faculty_junction_id.short_bio: Dr. Ramya Malur Srinivasan is a Senior Research Manager with Fujitsu Research, where she is a member of the AI Trust Research Center. Ramya’s background is in the areas of computer vision, machine learning, explainable AI, and AI ethics; with her research spanning diverse applications such as creativity, healthcare and finance.

faculty_id.title: AI Ethics and Fairness
faculty_id.description: Fairness is one of the most prominent values in the Ethics and Artificial Intelligence (AI) debate. This module provides an overview of the main account of fairness in AI and focuses on the need to pursue an ethical inquiry into the concept of fairness aimed at revising and enriching it, so as to design, develop and deploy really fair AI systems.
faculty_id.short_description: This module provides an overview of the main account of fairness in AI and focuses on the need to pursue an ethical inquiry into the concept of fairness aimed at revising and enriching it, so as to design, develop and deploy really fair AI systems.

faculty_junction_id.name: Benedetta Giovanola
faculty_junction_id.title: Full Professor of Ethics, Department of Political Sciences, Communication, and International Relations
faculty_junction_id.bio:
She is also a regular visiting professor at Tufts University (US). She has been visiting professor at the UIBE - University of International Economics and Business (Beijing, China), MGIMO (Moscow, Russia), KU Leuven (Belgium) and Huygens Fellow at the Radboud University Nijmegen (The Netherlands). She is currently the Vice President of the Italian Association for Moral Philosophy and the Director of a Lab on Cybersecurity in the framework of the Interuniversity National Consortium for Informatics in Italy. 

Her research interests are in business ethics, theories of justice, media ethics and the ethical questions raised by digital technologies and artificial intelligence, especially regarding fairness, social justice and inclusion, and with particular regard to the domain of health. She is/has been PI or member of a number of research projects on media ethics, digital ethics, and business ethics. She has given more than 100 talks in academic institutions in Europe, Asia and North America, has published 7 books and more than 120 articles in leading international journals and collections.
faculty_junction_id.short_bio: Benedetta Giovanola (Ph.D) holds the Jean Monnet Chair “Ethics for inclusive digital Europe” co-funded by the European Union and is Full Professor of Ethics at the University of Macerata (Italy), where she also served as Deputy Rector and Vice Rector for International Relations (2016-2022).

faculty_id.title: Online Age Verification: AI as a Solution?
faculty_id.description: In this lecture, Eynard unpacks the challenge of online age verification. She looks at the legal and technical frameworks which currently exist to protect minors, exploring how regulations by the European Union manifest in the national contexts of France and Germany. Through this exploration, she highlights the benefits and limitations of the current AI solutions. Eynard concludes her module with an outline of future considerations to govern online AI-powered age verification systems.
faculty_id.short_description: In this lecture, Jessica Eynard unpacks the challenge of online age verification.

faculty_junction_id.name: Jessica Eynard
faculty_junction_id.title: Associate Professor in Law
faculty_junction_id.bio:
Since 2019, she has served as co-director of the Master of Law, Digital, AI at the University of Toulouse Capitole. In addition, Jessica is a member of the chair in Law, Accountability and Social Trust in AI of the Artificial Intelligence Institute of Toulouse (ANITI). In 2012, she received the thesis award from the French Data Protection Authority (CNIL) for her thesis on the notion of personal data, published by Michalon.

Jessica has also directed the publication of a collective work on digital identity, published by Larcier in 2020, which received an award from the International Forum of Cybersecurity in 2021. She is currently co-editing two books: one on artificial intelligence (co-edited with Céline Castets-Renard, Professor at the University of Ottawa) and the other on self-sovereign digital identity (co-edited with Giorgia Macilotti, Researcher at the University of Toulouse Capitole).
faculty_junction_id.short_bio: Jessica Eynard is an Assistant Professor at the University of Toulouse Capitole in France. Her research interests include artificial intelligence law, digital identity and personal data protection law.

faculty_id.title: Governance “of, with and by” AI: a European perspective on the use and impact of AI in the public sector
faculty_id.description: In this module, Gianluca Misuraca explores the governance “of, with and by” AI, focusing on a European perspective on the use and impact of AI in the public sector. Misuraca divides his lecture into four parts: (1) Shaping Digital Europe 2040; (2) the trilemma of the Governance “of, with and by AI”; (3) AI in public services in the EU; and the EU approach to human-centric AI.
faculty_id.short_description: In this module, Gianluca Misura unpacks the European approach to the use of AI in the public sector.

faculty_junction_id.name: Gianluca Misuraca
faculty_junction_id.title: Founder and Vice President, Technology Diplomacy and International Relations
faculty_junction_id.bio:
He is also an advisor to several International Organizations, and development institutions worldwide. Among his key assignments he is currently leading, on behalf of the European Commission’s Service for Foreign Policy Instruments (FPI) and DG CONNECT, the multi-year facility support initiative “International Outreach for human-centric Artificial Intelligence” (InTouchAI.eu); and he is acting as Coordinator and Team Leader for the FPI funded support “ Digital Partnerships in Action” (DPA).

Among other several advisory activities, Gianluca has been Team leader for the design of the Multilateralism and Digitalisation Strategy for the European Commission’s DG INTPA, as well as coordinating the support on the digital analysis of the preparation of the Strategic Foresight Report on Green and Digital Transition 2050. In 2021 and 2022 he also provided support the Research and Innovation Team at ENISA in preparing their annual reports, with specific regard to Cybersecurity and Artificial Intelligence, mapping research and development in the field, identifying future trends and gaps to be addressed, as well as outlining policy recommendations.

As part of his academic roles, Gianluca is the Executive Director of the Master on Artificial
Intelligence in public services (AI4GOV) led by the Universidad Politécnica de Madrid, a Senior Research Associate at the Department of Design of Politecnico di Milano and a Research Fellow at the Department of eGovernance and Administration of Danube University Krems in Austria. Furthermore, he is a Special Advisor on Digital Public Administration for the Centre for Digital Economy (CED) and on Democracy in the Digital Age for Re-Imagine Europa (RIE).

Previously, Gianluca was a Senior Scientist at the European Commission's Joint Research Centre where, from 2009 to 2020, leading research and policy support in the field of Digital Government Transformation, Social Innovation and Artificial Intelligence for the public sector as part of the AI Watch. His educational background is economics and business administration, with focus on the interface between ICTs and public sector innovation. He holds a Diploma of Specialisation in High Level Studies in EU Economics and Law, an Executive Master in eGovernance and a PhD in Management of Technology from the Ecole Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL).
faculty_junction_id.short_bio: Gianluca Misuraca is founder and Vice President on Technology Diplomacy and International Relations of Inspiring Futures (IF), a global advisory consultancy in Strategic Foresight, Social Innovation and Digital Governance with headquarters in Lausanne and Seville.

faculty_id.title: AI and Ethics Dumping
faculty_id.description: This lecture introduces the listener to ‘ethics dumping’, and The TRUST Code–a global code of conduct for equitable research relationships. Two cases are provided: one where AI intended to improve the situation of the marginalized, but achieved the opposite, and one case of AI and ethics dumping. For beginners, an overview of AI ethics in 5 minutes is given at the start (thanks to Prof. Bernd Stahl and Dr. Kate Chatfield for providing comments on this clip). One clip of this lecture was produced for an ethics training app to be released by the PREPARED project in 2024 (funded by the European Commission under grant agreement 101058094).
faculty_id.short_description: This lecture introduces the listener to ‘ethics dumping’, and The TRUST Code–a global code of conduct for equitable research relationships.

faculty_junction_id.organization: University of Central Lancashire (UK) and Professor of Moral Philosophy, School of Law, University of Central Lancashire (Cyprus)
faculty_junction_id.name: Doris Schroeder
faculty_junction_id.title: Director of the Centre for Professional Ethics
faculty_junction_id.bio:
She was educated in Germany and the UK at postgraduate level in business / economics and philosophy / politics. Her first career was in management, as a budget planner for Time Warner. She has given invited presentations on all continents and in 28 countries. Previous employers include the University of Melbourne (Professorial Fellow), the University of Oslo and the University of Witwatersrand in Johannesburg.

Currently, Doris has a research-only post, which includes doctoral supervision. She has led a considerable number of competitive funding projects, including from the European Commission and the Wellcome Trust. Doris is the leading academic on 'ethics dumping', the export of unethical research practices from high to lower income regions. Her co-edited Ethics Dumping Case Studies (Springer, 2018) have been downloaded over 170,000 times. She is also the Lead Author of the Global Code of Conduct for Research in Resource-Poor Settings, which is being used in at least 50 countries. Her co-authored book on the code (Springer, 2019) has also been downloaded over 170,000 times.

Doris worked 17 years on a voluntary basis for Amnesty International. Her current research direction started after her PhD when she worked at the University of Witwatersrand in Johannesburg in 2000. Since then, her main research interests are focused on global justice, including benefit sharing and global research ethics. She has acted as a peer-reviewer for over 30 journals and publishers and currently has six editorial roles (e.g. with the Cambridge Quarterly of Healthcare Ethics and Research Ethics). She has been acting as an expert for the European Commission since 2004, including as a high-level expert directly reporting to the Director General for Research and Innovation. Other consultancy roles include regular assessor for the National Research Foundation South Africa, International Governing Board Member of the Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research and Medical Humanities Committee Member Wellcome Trust.
faculty_junction_id.short_bio: Doris Schroeder serves as the Director of the Centre for Professional Ethics, University of Central Lancashire (UK) and a Professor of Moral Philosophy, School of Law, University of Central Lancashire (Cyprus).

faculty_id.title: AI Governance and AI in Government
faculty_id.description: Today, governments are turning to the use of AI to improve their ‘GovTech’, the technology that is developed and used for their own functions and services. However, most policy and governance discussions on AI stick to questions about how big tech and the private sector’s development and use of AI must be governed. This module provides an overview of some ways governments are using AI in their own functions, the policies that they follow in this context, and some of the issues and concerns that come up with extensive use of AI in government, and particularly for citizen services.
faculty_id.short_description: This module provides an overview of some ways governments are using AI in their own functions, the policies that they follow in this context, and some of the issues and concerns around the extensive use of AI in government.

faculty_junction_id.name: Smitha Krishna Prasad
faculty_junction_id.title: Fritz Family Fellow
faculty_junction_id.bio:
Smitha is an Assistant Professor of law (on leave) at the National Law School of India University, Bangalore. She is also a Senior Research Fellow at the Digital Asia Hub, where she is involved in research related to the governance of digital infrastructure used to deliver public services, and more broadly digital platforms.

Smitha holds an LL.M. degree in International Legal Studies from the New York University School of Law, and a B.A.LL.B. from Symbiosis Law School, Pune.
faculty_junction_id.short_bio: Smitha is a Fritz Family Fellow with Georgetown’s Tech & Society Program and an SJD Candidate at Georgetown Law. Smitha’s primary research interests focus on issues around digital governance, privacy, data protection and surveillance. She also works on questions of emerging technology and law, and the expansion of tech regulation. Her current research focuses on policy and legal frameworks applicable in relation to the use of digital technologies in government functions and services, and the role that international organisations are playing in this context.
